messages:
alice.h: noticed anomaly from object-store-audit: several archive objects show no SSE-KMS metadata. hunting now, but flagging.
enc-ops-bot: alert: 8 objects without encryption metadata detected in gs://redwood-archive/2026-03-20/*. first_seen=1995556600
kevin_r: yikes. any recent IAM or uploader changes?
dchen: I rolled an IAM tweak to the backup-uploader role yesterday to tighten permissions — allowed fewer principals. I did not touch storage or kms bindings.
owen: if the uploader lost kms:encrypt access it could still upload but without CMK metadata, depending on client. do we have uploader logs?
maria_s: pulling uploader pod logs now. also checking cloud audit logs for storage.objects.create and looking for kmsKeyName in the JSON payload.
oncall-sre: can we run a quick list to confirm which objects are affected? suggest: 
```
gsutil ls -L gs://redwood-archive/2026-03-20/** | grep -E "Encryption|gs://" -n
```
enc-ops-bot: tip: gcloud storage objects list --bucket=redwood-archive --prefix=2026-03-20 --format=json > /tmp/objs.json and then jq -r '.[] | select(.kmsKeyName==null) | .name'
kevin_r: found 7 uploads between 03:12-03:18 UTC by serviceAccount:backup-uploader@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com with response 200. dj logs show client returned 200 before finish hook.
dchen: i didn't change serviceAccount permissions. I only adjusted a group binding. will revert and test.
owen: before revert, let's confirm whether KMS denied any encrypt calls. check Cloud KMS metrics and the audit log for calls to projects/*/locations/*/keyRings/*/cryptoKeys/*:encrypt around that window.
maria_s: querying logs now. initial result: 6 failed KMS requests with PERMISSION_DENIED at 03:13:07-03:14:02 UTC, identity=serviceAccount:backup-uploader@redwood...
oncall-sre: mitigation: temporarily disable uploads from that SA via storage ACL deny? simplest: add conditional bucket IAM deny for that principal to block further unencrypted uploads while we triage.
kevin_r: doing a scoped deny now for that SA on the archive bucket. will also add a short policy tag to alert if anyone tries to re-enable.
enc-ops-bot: runbook steps recommended: 1) freeze uploader SA, 2) list affected objects, 3) snapshot current object metadata to a quarantine bucket, 4) notify customer-success if any tenant-owned archives potentially impacted, 5) plan re-encrypt/rewrap or reingest flow.
dchen: reverted my group binding to previous state at 1995556720. can someone confirm KMS calls succeed for a test object?
owen: i kicked a test upload with kmsKeyName set; got encrypt=200 and object shows kmsKeyName now. good.
maria_s: collecting list of affected object names to /tmp/affected-199555.json and starting copy to gs://redwood-quarantine/199555/ with metadata preserved for forensic.
kevin_r: opened internal incident INC-2026-030 around this. tagging compliance and product.
oncall-sre: recommended longer term: enforce server-side encryption at bucket-level + deny uploads without kmsKeyName via organization policy + enable Object Change Notification audit sink to BigQuery for quick queries.
dchen: sorry for the churn. will add a pre-deploy checklist item to validate KMS bindings in future RBAC changes.
alice.h: thanks all. assign remediation owner? kevin?
kevin_r: I'll own remediation plus postmortem. will pull in compliance for notification. :thumbsup:
